sections.h2: How much is the city's cut of a New Braunfels tax bill?
sections.html:
The City of New Braunfels prints a 2025 total rate of $0.408936 per $100 of valuation. Debt service accounts for $0.193888 of the total, while $0.215048 goes to the General Fund for operations and maintenance.

The city's share is one component of the bill. Your school district, Comal County and any special districts bill separately, and Comal Appraisal District staff can confirm which ones reach your address. A rate newer than 2025 would appear on the city's Tax Information page.

sections.h2: Which offices appraise and collect in New Braunfels?
sections.html:
Comal Appraisal District sets the values from its Seguin Avenue office and takes calls at 830-625-8597, Monday through Friday. Collection runs through the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector, whom the city names as its partner and links from its tax page.

Texas government takes nothing in real estate tax itself. Value is pinned to January 1 and statements follow around October 1. If any part of your New Braunfels address lies in Guadalupe County, the Guadalupe County tax office is the one to ask.

  • Value, exemptions and protests: Comal Appraisal District.
  • Payment: the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector.
  • City hotel tax: the treasury office, 830-221-4369.
  • City main line: 830-221-4000.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in New Braunfels?
sections.html:
The bill is payable on arrival. By the Comptroller's reckoning, February 1 starts delinquency, and on that date the balance gains a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

Each later month adds another point of penalty until July, when it stops at twelve percent. Interest has no upper limit. If a taxing unit has hired a collection attorney, that attorney's charge can reach 20 percent.

  • Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, can pay in four slices.
  • Some collectors write repayment plans of up to 36 months; only a residence homestead is entitled to one.
  • Anyone asking to have the late charges forgiven needs a written request on file before day 181.

The lien arises each January 1, so whoever held title that morning owes the year, whatever happens to the deed afterward.

sections.h2: What exemptions are on offer for a New Braunfels homestead?
sections.html:
State law makes school districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead, with $60,000 more for older or disabled owners. Cities and counties may add theirs, and the amounts New Braunfels and Comal County grant are best confirmed with the appraisal district.

Headings on the district's exemptions page include:

  • Residence homestead, over-65, disabled person, and the surviving spouses of those owners.
  • Disabled veterans, including a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.
  • Heir property, the 11.35 disaster exemption, and tax deferral for owners 65 or older or disabled.
  • Pages on selling or buying a home that already has a homestead, and on losing the homestead cap.

Apply on Form 50-114, with most deadlines at April 30. Someone who buys after January 1 may take the exemption for the rest of that year when the seller held none. After a homestead is in place, appraised value can rise only 10 percent a year.

sections.h2: How do I contest a New Braunfels valuation?
sections.html:
Get your protest to the appraisal review board by May 15, or by day 30 after the notice reaches you when that is later. Homestead notices start around April 1.

Comal Appraisal District has a taxpayer liaison, reachable at 830-626-4874. If the board leaves the dispute unresolved, the next stops are district court or binding arbitration, plus the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000. Keep paying the undisputed part before February 1 so penalties do not stack during the appeal.

sections.h2: Can a New Braunfels house be used as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Rarely. A short-term rental here means a one- or two-family dwelling let for under 30 days, and the city's page bars the use in every residential zoning district, requires a special use permit in most non-residential districts, and keeps it out of the floodway.

This matters if your house has been advertised on a home-sharing site. Registration calls for a deed, a site plan, a floor plan, liability insurance of at least $500,000 per occurrence and a $206 fee that includes the first fire inspection. Renewal costs $128 and needs a Fire Marshal visit. No listing may be posted before the permit exists.

Since February 1, 2026 the city has routed hotel tax payments through an online portal called RentalScape, which handles filings for short-term rentals, hotels and resorts alike. Complaints about unpermitted rentals go to code compliance at 830-221-4074. Operators owe the city a hotel occupancy tax of 7 percent in addition to the state's 6 percent, filed by the 20th of each month even when nothing was earned, and late fees begin at $50. A buyer planning to rent the place should phone planning at 830-221-4050 and ask whether the address can be registered before signing.

sections.h2: How fast has New Braunfels grown?
sections.html:
QuickFacts describes a city that grew by roughly a third after the 2020 count:

  • Population: 122,492 by the July 2025 estimate, versus 90,403 in 2020 and 57,740 in 2010, a 35.5 percent rise on the 2020 base.
  • Land: 45.18 square miles, with 2,001.0 residents each in 2020.
  • Owners: 65.3 percent of occupied homes (2020-2024 survey), valued at $339,400 at the midpoint.
  • Costs per month: $2,088 with a mortgage, $745 without, and $1,654 gross rent.
  • Income: $86,021 at the median household, among 40,991 households.
  • Older residents: 14.9 percent are 65 or above.
  • Travel to work: 27.1 minutes.

The city's own tax page adds that sales and use tax totals 8.25 percent, of which the city keeps 1.5 percent.

sections.h2: What should a New Braunfels seller line up before listing?
sections.html:
Collect the paperwork that answers a buyer's first questions. Start with the latest tax statement for every unit that bills the house, and ask the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector for a current balance. Add your homestead exemption confirmation, since a buyer will have to file a fresh one.

  • If the house was ever rented for short stays, find the permit, the last fire inspection date and the final hotel tax return.
  • If a protest is pending, write down the hearing date so the buyer knows which value the tax will follow.
  • If the owner on record has died, talk to the title company early, because heirs not on a recorded deed must prove their interest to the appraisal district.

Because the population jumped after 2020, many nearby homes have sold recently, and the sale prices of comparable houses are what a protest hearing usually weighs.

faqs.q: What rate does New Braunfels print for 2025?
faqs.a: $0.408936 per $100 of valuation, split into $0.193888 for debt service and $0.215048 for operations.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property taxes to in New Braunfels?
faqs.a: The Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector takes payment, per the city. For value or exemption questions, call the Comal Appraisal District at 830-625-8597.

faqs.q: Is a short-term rental allowed in a New Braunfels residential zone?
faqs.a: No. The city bars them in every residential district. Other districts mostly require a special use permit plus a yearly fire inspection.

faqs.q: When do New Braunfels property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: They turn delinquent on February 1, when a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added, with the penalty ending at 12 percent in July.

faqs.q: Must a buyer reapply for the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. File Form 50-114 with the Comal Appraisal District, because the exemption on record belongs to the January 1 owner. After that date a buyer may claim it for the rest of the year if the seller had none.
